applies_to: Biomedical Engineering / Biomedizinische Technik research article

sources.name: BMT Instructions for Authors, Equations and symbols
exact_requirements: Equations should be well-aligned and not crowded.
Avoid complicated superscripts and subscripts by introducing new symbols.
For MS Word submissions, create equations using the Microsoft equation editor or a corresponding add-on.
Do not submit math equations as images, but as editable text.
Number displayed equations consecutively with Arabic numerals (if referred to in the text).

sources.name: NIST Typefaces for Symbols in Scientific Manuscripts
applied_rules: Quantity and variable symbols are italic.
Explicitly defined functions/operators and descriptive terms are roman.
Descriptive subscripts/superscripts are roman; running variable indices are italic.

sources.name: Microsoft: Write an equation or formula in Word
sources.exact_quote: The Professional option displays the equation in a professional format optimized for display.

editorial_choices_not_BMT_mandates: Only three principal method equations in the main text and two diagnostic-decomposition equations in the supplement.
Centered single-line display mathematics and right-aligned parenthesized labels.
Cambria Math native Word equations, main12pt/supplement11pt, with upright descriptive labels.
Symmetric borderless equation-layout containers carry true m:oMathPara; these containers are not scientific data tables.
selection_rationale: Dice defines agreement, and the two risks define the compared methods. Only the two less-standard Kitagawa component definitions warrant supplemental display. Routine arithmetic and named standard statistical procedures are retained in precise prose and cited code, without a new mathematical appendix.
